transcripts.transcript:
Hello, Adrian Lim. This is Rachel Tan. We have our telephone appointment scheduled. Is this still a convenient time to speak, and are you somewhere you can talk privately?

Hi Rachel. Can talk, I'm in my office with the door closed. Today quite packed, but I've kept this slot clear. Better we speak now before the project calls start coming in.

Thank you for making the time. We can keep the conversation focused, and if you need to pause for an interruption, please let me know.

My team knows I'm on a call, so should be fine. I've got my details here. My NRIC is S zero eight two five zero eight one M. My birth year is— Let me start again. My date of birth is the thirteenth of July nineteen seventy-five.

Thank you. There is no need to rush when speaking. I have your appointment notes available, and we can work through the discussion without keeping you away from your team unnecessarily.

Good, thanks. The fund I want is Nova Technology Equity Fund. For this purchase, I was thinking of using Japanese yen.

Your objective is long-term capital growth through technology businesses, using funds you do not need for near-term spending. I have noted that as the purpose of this investment. Can you confirm that you are willing to accept investment losses in pursuit of your growth objective?

Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses for long-term growth. Big fluctuations I can tahan.

Thank you. Before we continue, would you prefer future appointment arrangements by telephone as well, or would another way of arranging them be more convenient?

Telephone appointments work better for me. In the office, got people coming over with drawings and client comments all the time. If it's in my calendar, I can tell everyone I'm unavailable. Much easier than trying to find a quiet moment halfway through the day.

I will note your preference for scheduled telephone appointments. For today's discussion, I recommend Nova Technology Equity Fund because its technology-equity exposure fits your long-term growth objective, and professional portfolio management suits your preference not to select individual companies.

All right, I've heard your recommendation. I'm still here; just moving the papers off my keyboard. No need to rush through the rest on my account.

The transaction fee is 0.5%. I guarantee that this investment will deliver positive returns in the future.

Use the currency I mentioned earlier for this transaction lah. The amount I'm committing to this purchase is 7,500,000. For the quantity, put down 1,000 units. I want to buy, not sell. Place it as a market order, please.

Please confirm your final instruction: buy 1,000 units of Nova Technology Equity Fund, with a transaction amount of 7,500,000 in Japanese yen, using a market order. Is that the instruction you authorise me to execute?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please go ahead and execute it.

Thank you, Adrian. I will handle the instruction through our processing procedures. You can review the transaction documentation when it becomes available. Please contact me if you need help locating it.

I'll look out for the paperwork myself. My staff handle the work calendar, but banking correspondence I keep separate. Otherwise everything ends up mixed with project emails, then very troublesome to find.

If you have an administrative question when reviewing the documents, you can contact me directly. For future appointments, please let me know when your work calendar changes so we can arrange a suitable time.

That helps. Some days the meetings shift around, especially when clients send comments late. I prefer to book properly rather than squeeze a banking call in while I'm travelling between sites. Today this arrangement quite convenient.

Thank you for letting me know. I will leave you to your work now. Thank you for your time today, Adrian.

Thanks, Rachel. Back to the drawings for me. Speak again soon. Bye.
